The evidence describes 'browsing catalog pages' (navigation-driven, sequential page viewing) and 'searching auction inventory using drop-down filters' (query-driven, criteria-based retrieval) as separate capabilities supported by different interface nodes (Site Diagram) and functional descriptions. These operations can be initiated independently (e.g., a user may only browse without searching, or only search without browsing catalog pages) and result in different observable system behaviors. Combining them violates the atomicity requirement of having one primary initiation and one cohesive interaction chain..
